ordered_diagnoses: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas

s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased
Family history of similar facial papules
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules are present on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Lesions gradually increased to approximately 60
Patient has a medical history of meningioma
Family history is notable for a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

shortlist: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas

shortlist.label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, and a medical history of meningioma, which are characteristic features of this syndrome

shortlist.label: Gorlin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, this condition also presents with multiple basal cell carcinomas, and the patient's family history of similar facial papules supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces, which is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Generalized Basaloid Follicular Hamartoma Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's multiple skin-colored papules and family history of similar lesions are consistent with this rare genetic disorder

shortlist.label: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's multiple lesions and family history of similar papules, combined with the histopathological findings, make this diagnosis a plausible consideration

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, along with a history of meningioma and a family history of similar lesions, combined with the histopathological findings and the genetic mutation in the SUFU gene, are all consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (also known as Gorlin Syndrome). The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, which is a known genetic alteration associated with this syndrome, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gorlin Syndrome
rejected.why: Gorlin Syndrome is another name for Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, so it is not a distinct alternative

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: While the histopathology shows features consistent with infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma, the overall clinical presentation and genetic findings are more consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome

rejected.label: Generalized Basaloid Follicular Hamartoma Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a different set of clinical and histopathological features, and is not associated with the same genetic mutations

rejected.label: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas
rejected.why: While this condition shares some similarities with the patient's presentation, the presence of a meningioma and the specific genetic mutation in the SUFU gene are more consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome
